text: Volcanic and other such activity at the mid-Atlantic ridge extrudes material to fill the gap between separating tectonic plates associated with continental drift. The magnetization of rocks is found to reverse in a coordinated manner with distance from the ridge. What does this imply about the Earth’s magnetic field and how could the knowledge of the spreading rate be used to give its historical record?
Explain why two magnetic field lines cannot cross. What would a crossing imply about the direction of the magnetic field at that point?

Compare and contrast electric field lines and magnetic field lines. Describe at least two similarities and two differences. At least one similarity and one difference should concern how the fields interact with matter.

Noting that the magnetic field lines of a bar magnet resemble the electric field lines of a pair of equal and opposite charges, do you expect the magnetic field to rapidly decrease in strength with distance from the magnet? Is this consistent with your experience with magnets?

Is Earth’s magnetic field parallel to the ground everywhere? Where is its strength generally greatest? Explain why a compass needle constrained to rotate horizontally becomes unreliable near a magnetic pole, even though the magnetic field there is strong.
If a charged particle moves in a straight line through some region of space, can you say that the magnetic field in that region is necessarily zero?

The knocking sounds heard during an MRI scan come largely from vibrations of current-carrying gradient coils in the scanner’s main magnetic field. At one instant, a straight 5.0-cm segment of wire in a gradient coil carries a current of 100 A perpendicular to a 1.5-T magnetic field. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force on this segment at that instant?

A wire carrying a 30.0-A current passes between the poles of a strong magnet that is perpendicular to its field and experiences a 2.16-N force on the 4.00 cm of wire in the field. What is the average field strength?

In Faraday’s two-coil apparatus, why does the galvanometer briefly register a current when the switch is closed, but return to zero while the switch remains closed? What happens when the switch is opened again?

An ideal plug-in transformer supplies 9.00 V to a video game system. (a) How many turns are in its secondary coil if its input voltage is 120 V and the primary coil has 400 turns? (b) What is its input current when its output current is 1.30 A?

A traveler carries a transformer to convert a 240-V AC supply to 120 V for an appliance. Treat the transformer as ideal. (a) What is the ratio of turns in its primary and secondary coils? (b) What is the ratio of input to output current? (c) How could the same transformer be used to obtain 240 V from a 120-V AC supply?

A real transformer delivers less electrical power than it receives. Explain how electrical resistance in the coils and eddy currents induced in the iron core contribute to this inefficiency. Why does constructing the core from thin iron sheets separated by insulating layers reduce energy loss?

A transformer increases the voltage used to transmit a given amount of electrical power. How does this affect the current in the transmission lines? Explain why this reduces energy loss in lines whose resistance stays the same.
Give an example of a use of AC power other than in the household. Similarly, give an example of a use of DC power other than that supplied by batteries.
Why do voltage, current, and power go through zero 120 times per second for 60-Hz AC electricity?
You are riding in a train, gazing into the distance through its window. As close objects streak by, you notice that the nearby fluorescent lights make dashed streaks. Explain.
Military aircraft use 400-Hz AC power, because it is possible to design lighter-weight equipment at this higher frequency. What is the time for one complete cycle of this power?
